newsitem.title: USA: BASKETBALL NBA-JAZZ, STOCKTON AGREE ON NEW DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL NBA-JAZZ, STOCKTON AGREE ON NEW DEAL.

text.p: Point guard John Stockton, the NBA's all-time leader in assists and steals, is staying with Karl Malone and the Utah Jazz.
Stockton, 34, agreed to a three-year contract at undisclosed terms. The Salt Lake Tribune reported Tuesday the deal is worth $15 million.
The two-time Olympic gold medalist will not sign the deal until October 4, when he gets back in town for the start of training camp.
"We're pleased things have worked out and John plans to sign what will likely be his final NBA contract with the Jazz," Jazz owner Larry Miller told the paper.
"He has contributed more to this franchise than numbers alone will ever tell. When I think of John Stockton, the word that personifies him most is thoroughbred."
The eight-time All-Star, who won gold for the 1992 and 1996 Dream Teams, is a 12-year veteran who has missed just four games in his career.
But he has never won an NBA championship.
The Stockton-Malone duo, one of the most potent in league history, has helped the Jazz to three Western Conference finals, but the Jazz have never played in the Finals.
Stockton did not miss a game last season and averaged 14.7 points and 11.2 assists.

In his 980-game career, the gritty guard has averaged 13.6 points and 11.5 assists per game. Stockton's best season was 1989-90, when he established a career high with 14.5 assists per game and matched a career standard by scoring 17.2.
